# Course as Runnable Study Tool

Four separate courses were revised by **building the syllabus into a program** rather than by reading
notes. Same architecture every time, in four unrelated repositories. This is the most distinctive
habit in the source set that no single repo reveals.

## The four instances

| Repo | App | Scale |
|---|---|---|
| `IT Applications in Business and Commerce` | `lecture/exam_prep/` | 497 questions, 28 sets, generated bank |
| `Physics` | `exam_prep/` | 29 topics, 13 canvas simulators, 82 Leitner flashcards, 75-question bank, transcribed exam with worked solutions |
| `Optimization Methods` | `exam_prep/` | 24 chapters, 5 modules, 23 canvas demos, glossary |
| `Information-Systems-Modelling` | `ism_final_exam_prep/` | 570 questions |

## Lineage, not parallel invention

> "One was first and I copied it forward."
> — interview, 2026-07-28

The origin is **`IT Applications in Business and Commerce`**. Worth one caveat for honesty: the
earliest *in-repo* timestamp evidence points elsewhere — `Physics/exam_prep/js/*` carries mtimes of
2026-06-27→06-30, weeks before the others appear in any tree. The quiz app in IT Applications has no
comparable in-repo timestamp because that project's development history lives in a different
repository, so the mtime ordering cannot settle it either way. The interview is treated as
authoritative here; the mtime observation is recorded rather than dropped.

## The shared architecture

Every instance, independently:

- **No build step, no dependencies, opens from `file://`** — see [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]]
- Plain HTML + CSS + vanilla JS; data, logic and presentation in separate files
- `localStorage` progress with a **`STORAGE_VERSION` integer** that invalidates saved state on schema
  change (IT Applications is at version 7 — six prior breaks implied)
- Hash-based routing and deep links to a single chapter
- **Canvas demos** rather than static figures: 13 physics simulators, 23 optimisation demos
- A **hand-rolled test harness** using `node:vm` plus a DOM shim, loading the *production* JS and
  driving real event handlers — `Physics/exam_prep/tools/qa.mjs`,
  `IT Applications.../lecture/exam_prep/qa_test.js`
- A **generated question bank with its pristine source kept beside it** — see
  [[generated-artifact-with-pristine-source]]

## Why the shape recurs

The constraint is the exam room, not the browser: revision has to work with no network, on any
machine, at any hour. That produces the same design pressure as
[[offline-first-static-deliverable]], and the two patterns share their whole toolbox.

## Evidence

> "It's a single-page web app written in plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript — **no build step, no server, no
> dependencies, no internet**. Open one file and start revising."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/ism_final_exam_prep/README.md, 2026-07-09

> "No build step. No server. No internet. **Open one HTML file and start revising.**"
> — Physics/README.md, 2026-07-10

Two repositories, five months apart, reaching for nearly the same sentence.

## What the tools verify, and what they do not

The harnesses are real — `qa_test.js` exits non-zero on failure, `qa.mjs` runs 34 static checks
including "every file loaded by `index.html` is precached by the service worker". What none of them
check is **subject-matter correctness**: `Physics` claims its Bohr simulator reproduces the Balmer
lines, but `qa.mjs` validates ids, assets and KaTeX parsing, never numerical output. The pedagogical
claims rest on prose. See [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].

`Physics` did catch two answer-key errors in a provided exam set — recorded in its own generated
audit, unconfirmed with the lecturer. `TODO:` whether the tool was used for the exam is recorded at
medium confidence only; the interview did not state it outright.
